how: Successor-canvas activity does not establish a collectively accepted lasting purpose when members explicitly disagree about whether the subreddit still has a use.
Reporting other people on a successor canvas establishes an available destination rather than this room's collective migration.
The banner request and moderator's CSS response establish intention but cannot establish actual implementation.
Successor-canvas work is evidenced for one reporting participant without establishing a collective migration or its durability.
A joking proposal does not establish a collective decision or an implemented emblem change.
Replacement proposals and one proposer's completed flag establish individual continuation but not collective adoption or lasting organization.
Concrete starting instructions establish a proposed continuation but not a completed successor mark.
Remaking the canvas characters begins during active placement, before the model's near-close timing.
Reported continuation coexists with refusal, leaving collective agreement and successor-canvas uptake unresolved.
Future preparation remains wishes and proposals rather than demonstrated implementation on another canvas.
Flair during active placing establishes findability rather than after-close emblem retention, which is supported separately by the later header observation.
Continuation proposals do not establish an accomplished migration or completed successor drawing without evidence of follow-through.
Keeping cross-fandom ties can originate during active placement rather than only near or after closure.
Offering a successor does not establish adoption or continued collective work there.
Extension of ties begins during placement here, requiring broader timing and a distinction between proposals, promises, observed arrivals and lasting relationships.
Reuse can begin during live placement rather than only near or after the close
Sharing a timelapse is recording and does not alone demonstrate remaking the work in another material
The supported transition is an individual pre-close proposal to reuse a canvas figure, leaving collective adoption unresolved.
Only the Kiwi reuse proposal supports proposed emblem adoption, while the naming question and salute proposal do not inherit that canvas meaning.
The closure rule must be scoped to the original canvas because successor creation and placement mistakes are reported after it ends.
Collective continuation requires evidence beyond an individual's redirect to another canvas.
The continuation invitation does not establish migration uptake or durable organizational continuity.
Conditional interest in successor canvases must remain distinct from a demonstrated venue choice or migration.
Visible preservation and restart proposals do not establish a completed atlas entry, collective uptake or durable continuation.
Evidence of individual rebuilding cannot establish an enduring collective, and deleted-body titles cannot resolve who joined or what persisted off site.
Parallel continuation begins during the original canvas cooldown rather than only near or after its closure.
The theme's introduction routing occurred during the event, so only its later appearance work establishes post-event regrouping.
An invitation to a successor canvas does not establish collective uptake or successful work there.
Successor work claims and proposals support continuation in talk without proving editability or completion of later additions.
Two turns from one author establish an invitation rather than a successful transfer of collective work.
